story.title: Fatal Incident on Six Flags Roller Coaster Leads to Ride Closures
story.summary: A man named Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was killed after being ejected from the 'Goliath' roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. He reportedly struck other patrons during his fall before landing below. Following this incident, Six Flags announced the temporary closure of nine other roller coasters across its parks in North America as a precautionary measure. The incident is currently under investigation.

explore_lenses.label: What do investigators still need to determine?
explore_lenses.title: The cause of the ejection is not established
explore_lenses.summary: Police have confirmed an ejection and resulting injuries, but have not identified why it occurred. The local criminal-investigations unit and Georgia's ride-safety regulator are conducting separate active reviews.

claims.text: Cobb County police say preliminary witness and employee interviews indicate Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was ejected, struck other patrons, and fell beneath the attraction; investigators are still examining the circumstances.
Georgia's Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire said its team is conducting an in-depth review to determine the circumstances and compliance with applicable policies and procedures.
No authority has publicly determined whether the fatal ejection resulted from a restraint problem, another equipment issue, operations, rider conduct, or another cause.

explore_lenses.label: Why were nine rides closed across the chain?
explore_lenses.title: A precaution extended beyond the Georgia park
explore_lenses.summary: Six Flags shut nine high-speed, large-scale coasters at six parks in the United States and Canada after the fatal incident. The action is precautionary and does not itself establish that any of those rides has a defect.

claims.text: The company temporarily closed Nitro, Raging Bull, Behemoth, Leviathan, Goliath at Magic Mountain, Fury 325, Thunder Striker, Orion, and Diamondback after the Georgia incident.
Six Flags said guest and employee safety remains a top priority; separately, the company told local media it was cooperating fully with authorities and supporting affected guests and team members.

Eight of the nine closed rides were made by Bolliger & Mabillard; the closed Goliath at Magic Mountain was made by Giovanola. Bolliger & Mabillard said it was actively investigating and would not comment further until it better understood what happened.
Neither Six Flags nor investigators have announced a reopening date or linked the closures to a confirmed common mechanical cause.

explore_lenses.label: What safety actions can Georgia require next?
explore_lenses.title: State rules allow inspections and ordered shutdowns
explore_lenses.summary: Georgia's safety regulator oversees amusement-ride safety and has authority to inspect, order a ride out of service when it is hazardous or unsafe, and require corrective conditions before it resumes operation.

claims.text: Georgia rules assign amusement-ride safety administration to the Safety Engineering Section of the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire.

Under those rules, the state may order a temporary cessation of operations after an inspection finds a ride hazardous or unsafe; operations cannot resume until conditions are corrected to the agency's satisfaction.

The rules require stationary amusement rides to be state-inspected before first public operation and at least annually, while owners must arrange a qualified daily inspection and test before normal operation each day.
Whether Georgia will issue a formal shutdown order, require repairs or operational changes, or find violations is unresolved pending the state's review.

story_report.summary: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was killed after he was ejected from the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, according to Cobb County police. Preliminary interviews with witnesses and employees indicated that he struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction. Authorities and Georgia safety officials are investigating the circumstances. In an immediate precautionary response, Six Flags temporarily closed nine other roller coasters across its North American parks.

sections.heading: Police and State Safety Reviews
sections.body: Cobb County police are continuing to examine the fatal incident, while Georgia’s Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire is conducting an in-depth review of the circumstances and compliance with applicable policies and procedures. Six Flags said it was cooperating with authorities and supporting affected guests and employees. The company also said guest and employee safety remained a top priority.

sections.heading: Six Flags Expands Ride Closures
sections.body: The temporary closures cover Nitro, Raging Bull, Behemoth, Leviathan, Goliath at Magic Mountain, Fury 325, Thunder Striker, Orion and Diamondback. Eight of those rides were made by Bolliger & Mabillard, which said it was actively investigating; Goliath at Magic Mountain was made by Giovanola. The company has not publicly detailed the selection criteria beyond describing the rides as similar hypercoasters.

sections.heading: Georgia Amusement Ride Safety Rules
sections.body: Georgia assigns amusement-ride safety administration to the Safety Engineering Section of the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire. State rules require inspections of stationary rides before their first public operation and at least annually, as well as qualified daily inspections and tests before normal operation. If an inspection finds a ride hazardous or unsafe, the state may order operations halted until corrective conditions are met.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not publicly determined whether the ejection involved a restraint problem, another equipment issue, operations, rider conduct or another cause; police and state findings, patron injury conditions and inspection results have not been released.
Neither Six Flags nor investigators has announced a reopening date, confirmed a common mechanical cause for the nine closures, or announced a final state inspection finding or enforcement action.

related_stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case involving the Trump administration's claim that records related to Elon Musk's DOGE are exempt from Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requirements. The administration argues that DOGE qualifies as a presidential advisory body, thus limiting public access to its records.

related_stories.title: Bryan Cranston Pays Tribute to RJ Mitte Following His Death at 34
related_stories.summary: Bryan Cranston expressed deep sorrow over the death of his 'Breaking Bad' co-star RJ Mitte, who passed away at the age of 34. Cranston referred to Mitte as 'my sweet son' and revealed they had been planning to meet for lunch shortly before his death. Mitte's representative confirmed that he died by suicide at his home in Brownsville, Texas.
